- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 2–5% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates in early horizon (1–5 days) after a price drop; reduce forecast by 2–4% for first 3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.3 in last 5 days → model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is rising, model often misses momentum; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3 days.
- Model tends to underestimate late horizon (20–30 days) after a strong upward move; add 2–4% to forecast for final 5–7 days.
